label: PF Backlog 646
title: intake-builds stores: ingest into DB metadata + object store (EDP-24 gap)

decisions.note: Gate 1.5 sha 56ded4e61ef1: AC2 ref corrected to artifacts, backfill_status added, artifact id derivation pinned, cross-tenant test added, CLI secrets via env only, gate0 fix split.

brief.problem: 11 intake/builds files stay outside the DB/object model.
brief.what_adds: Ingest with sha256 into the object store and register metadata.
brief.success: Registry flips to migrated after parity.

objective: Ingest the 11 non-legacy intake-raw/builds stores into the EDP object store and artifact metadata (tenant-scoped, checksum-verified, idempotent) and move their store-registry targets to the existing artifact substrate with an honest backfill_status; the legacy-dashboard product_forge_context.json stays planned.
acceptance_criteria: A Go ingestion service and CLI compute sha256 for each intake/builds file, write the bytes to the object store under a content-addressed key, and register a tenant-scoped stored_objects row plus an artifacts row; re-running unchanged input reuses the same artifact id and creates no additional rows.

store-registry targets for exactly the 11 non-legacy intake/builds entries (conversations, ideas, requirements, decisions, change_packages, implementation_plans, discovery-panel, items.jsonl, intake-files, build-info, version) move from object-store/planned to object-store/exists with ref=artifacts, owner_item=BI-PF-1475 and migration_status=migrated; each target also records backfill_status=pending plus the pfingest command, and the legacy-dashboard product_forge_context.json stays planned.

Tests prove: idempotent re-ingest (stable artifact id and row counts); checksum verification against the object store; a changed payload yields a NEW artifact id/revision while the prior object stays readable; and a second tenant cannot read the first tenant's artifact (RLS non-leakage).

pfingest --verify exits non-zero and names each store when the source file checksum, the artifacts checksum, or the object-store checksum disagree (Head when it surfaces sha256, otherwise a streamed re-hash); the JSON report uses the pinned schema pf.intake-ingest/1 with run_id (UUIDv4), per-file status (written|skipped-unchanged|drift|failed), duration and byte counts.
in_scope: go/intakeingest service + tests (idempotent ingest, changed-payload revision, checksum verification, cross-tenant non-leakage)
config/store-registry.json: flip the 11 targets with backfill_status + ingest_writer
out_of_scope: Running the production backfill or moving file producers off files (per-domain cutover); the exact pfingest command is recorded per target.
Schema changes, GC of orphaned objects (reported for objreconcile), and live/staging ingestion in CI.
approach: Add a Go ingestion service (go/intakeingest) over the existing datastore.ObjectStore + RelationalStore ports. For each source file it computes sha256, writes bytes under intake/<sha256> or builds/<sha256> with Immutable=true, then upserts stored_objects (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and artifacts (id=sha256(tenant|bucket|logical_name|checksum)[:32], ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, revision=next per tenant+name) inside one RLS-bound transaction. A thin cmd/pfingest wires PF_RUNTIME_DSN/PF_OBJECT_ROOT/tenant, prints the pinned pf.intake-ingest/1 JSON report, enforces a per-file size cap, and --verify re-reads the source, compares source/artifacts/Head checksums, and exits non-zero on drift. The 11 registry targets move to artifacts/exists/migrated with owner_item BI-PF-1475, ingest_writer go/intakeingest and backfill_status pending (historical parity is an explicit ops run, never silently claimed); STORE-DATAFLOW is regenerated. Gate 1.5 hardening: object keys are tenant-prefixed; artifact revision allocation uses a bounded insert-with-conflict-retry on uq_artifacts_name_revision (no read-max race); pfingest refuses to run as a BYPASSRLS/superuser role unless --allow-bypassrls is explicit; --verify falls back to streaming and re-hashing when Head does not surface sha256; the pf.intake-ingest/1 report carries run_id UUIDv4, duration, bytes and written|skipped-unchanged|drift|failed per file, is written to stdout and optionally --report-file for scheduled runs; --dry-run shows planned writes without mutating; transient failures retry with bounded backoff then fail closed.

prior_decisions: BI-PF-1408 Slice A/B/C: every store classified, mapped to a target, and relationship-checked; 12 intake/builds stores remain pending. Slice C flips planned->exists once the target substrate and owner item exist.
BI-PF-1307/EDP-15: artifacts metadata lives in Postgres (artifacts) and bytes live in the object store keyed by checksum (stored_objects).
EDP single-storage standard (BI-PF-1417): no new store/table; reuse the existing artifact substrate.
Legacy dashboard is frozen and not architecture authority; product_forge_context.json stays with its legacy owner.
Gate 1.5 review (sha 56ded4e61ef1) requires registry sequencing, artifact-id semantics, module reuse, cross-tenant tests, observability and ownership to be explicit.

assumptions: The 11 in scope are the 12 currently pending intake/builds entries minus the legacy-dashboard product_forge_context.json (Gate 1 approved).
The operator supplies the tenant id at the CLI boundary; ingestion is an admin/ops action, not a public API.
The logical artifact name is the bucket-relative source path; content addressing makes re-ingest idempotent.
Registry 'exists' means the target substrate + single writer exist; historical-data parity is tracked separately by backfill_status, so the registry never claims data that was not ingested.
Object keys are tenant-prefixed (tenant/<tenant>/intake|builds/<sha256>), so the raw object layer cannot be cross-read by key even before RLS; the object root is never served directly to clients.

The ingestion process runs as a non-BYPASSRLS role; pfingest preflights pg_roles.rolbypassrls for current_user and refuses to run when it is true unless --allow-bypassrls is passed for an isolated local test DB.
Revision allocation is a bounded insert-with-conflict-retry on the unique (tenant,name,revision) index, so concurrent writers cannot duplicate a revision.
divergences: The stale derived affected_files suggested scripts/dev/ingest_intake.py; the language rule requires new shipped logic in Go, so the ingestion path is go/intakeingest + cmd/pfingest (Gate 1 approved).

AC2 wording was corrected after Gate 1.5: ref is the OBJECT_META target artifacts (not the logical bucket name), and each target carries backfill_status so exists does not over-claim historical parity.

impact_review.evidence: New ingestion logic and tests are Go (go/intakeingest); registry/docs changes are declarative JSON/Markdown; the gate0 path fix is tooling Python.

Reuses artifacts + stored_objects (BI-PF-1307), objstore, datastore ports and store.BindTenant; no new table or store. go/intakeingest/go.mod requires productforge/datastore, objstore and store via replace => ../<module>, matching artifacts/go.mod.
Writes run through store.BindTenant (RLS app.tenant_id); artifacts/stored_objects carry tenant_id; the integration test ingests as tenant A and asserts tenant B sees nothing.

Object keys are content-addressed and immutable; stored_objects uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; artifact id = sha256(tenant|bucket|logical_name|checksum)[:32], so unchanged input maps to the same id (DO NOTHING) while changed bytes map to a new id + next revision and leave the old object readable.

Source-file owners (conversation_models, build_manager, version_manager, discovery_panel, intake_channels, intake_files) keep the files; go/intakeingest is the single writer of the derived object/artifacts copies under prefixes intake/ and builds/, recorded on each registry target as ingest_writer.

Pinned JSON report pf.intake-ingest/1 with run_id, per-file written|skipped|drift|failed, counts, and a per-store log line; --verify exits non-zero on any mismatch; orphaned content-addressed objects are reported for objreconcile.
No schema change; per-file --max-bytes cap (default 256MiB) fails closed; metadata failure leaves a harmless content-addressed object that a retry reuses; rollback is a revert.

Keys are tenant-prefixed; the object root is never public; reads go through the RLS-bound service; a second tenant's artifact lookup returns ErrNotFound and a direct key probe outside the tenant prefix fails.
Revision is allocated by insert-with-conflict-retry on uq_artifacts_name_revision; same checksum+name maps to the same deterministic id and is a no-op.
pfingest preflights current_user's rolbypassrls and superuser flags and refuses by default; the cross-tenant test runs on the runtime DSN, so a bypass role fails the test instead of silently passing.
Bounded retry with backoff for transient DB/object errors; after exhaustion the run exits non-zero with per-file failed status; a metadata failure leaves a reusable content-addressed object.

risks: Object write succeeds but metadata write fails: mitigated by content-addressed immutable objects, idempotent retry (no duplicate rows), and orphan reporting for objreconcile.
Tenant misconfiguration could mix intake data: mitigated by a required explicit tenant, RLS via store.BindTenant, and a fail-able cross-tenant test.
Large intake files: mitigated by a per-file --max-bytes cap (default 256MiB) that fails closed instead of truncating.
Registry over-claiming historical data: mitigated by backfill_status=pending on every flipped target plus pfingest --verify parity.
rollback: Revert the commit; content-addressed objects are safe to leave in place and no schema change is made.

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=56ded4e61ef1
BLOCKER:
  - Registry flips to exists/migrated in this commit while live ingestion is explicitly out of scope: shipped state asserts 11 stores have objects/rows that will not exist until ops later runs `pfingest`, so `pfingest --verify` and any existence check contradict `store-registry.json` on day one. Design must sequence: ingest + verify first, flip registry only on proof of existence.
  - Artifact revision semantics are unresolved: "deterministic id + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING" cannot both satisfy "same artifact id on unchanged input" and "changed payload produces a new object while prior stays readable" unless the id derivation (path vs path+sha) is stated; if path-derived, `DO NOTHING` permanently pins the artifacts row to the old checksum.
MAJOR:
  - AC conformance mismatch: acceptance criteria require the 11 entries marked "object-store/exists with migration_status migrated"; the approach flips them to "artifacts/exists/migrated". Repeated AC-wording drift class — reconcile explicitly before Gate 1.5.
  - `go/intakeingest/go.mod` as a new module over "existing datastore.ObjectStore + RelationalStore ports": state where those ports live; if they are in the repo's root Go module this forces duplication (reuse violation) or a `replace` directive (version drift across modules).
  - Tenant/RLS isolation is claimed (BindTenant, RLS-bound tx) but no test is listed for cross-tenant non-leakage; a claimed security control without a fail-able test is unproven (checklist 9, 6).
  - Observability is a printed JSON report only: no per-store structured success/failure log, no run record, no metric distinguishing written vs skipped vs failed, so a half-failed 11-store run cannot be diagnosed or later proven ingested (checklist 10).
  - CL-001 ownership not stated: who else writes `stored_objects`/`artifacts`, and is this writer registered as single-writer for intake|builds keys? No route-by-kind/ownership disposition present.
  - CL-006 not addressed: this Gate-1 context does not embed the latest Gate 1.5 findings + dispositions, which `scripts/dev/gate1_check.py` enforces as a precondition for approval.
MINOR:
  - DSN passed via `cmd/pfingest` wiring risks credential exposure in argv/shell history; specify env-var/secret-file intake.
  - "Configurable size cap" appears in risks but not in the design: no config key, default, or scope (per-file vs total) defined, and no fail-closed evidence test listed.
  - `--verify` comparison basis unstated: Head checksum vs freshly re-read local file, and behaviour when the source file changed after ingest.
  - `gate0_check.py` git-root fix is a real correctness fix but bundles an unrelated tooling concern with the ingestion change; split for reviewability and independent rollback.
  - No GC/retention story for orphaned content-addressed objects when object write succeeds and metadata write fails (risk acknowledged but unmanaged).
NIT:
  - Pipe delimiter in `intake|builds/<sha256>` object keys: confirm it is safe/documented across the object store and any path-based tooling.
  - JSON report schema is not pinned/versioned; ops automation parsing it will break silently on field changes.
  - Deterministic artifact id derivation should be recorded in an ADR/store-registry comment so future writers compute identical ids.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid foundations: Go-first logic, content-addressed immutability, RLS-bound transactions, and idempotent upserts are the right shape, and rollback is clean (no schema change).
  - Top risks: registry claims "exists/migrated" before any ingestion actually runs (integrity), and artifact-id/`DO NOTHING` revision semantics are underspecified against AC 3.
  - Secondary gaps: separate Go module reuse strategy, missing cross-tenant test, print-only observability, and unembedded CL-006/CL-001 process evidence.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=c87c1027d1af
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Object keys `intake/<sha256>`/`builds/<sha256>` are global, not tenant-prefixed: isolation depends solely on metadata RLS; any actor with raw PF_OBJECT_ROOT read access can cross-tenant read. Need an explicit statement that object-layer access is only via the RLS-bound service, plus a test for direct-key non-leakage.
  - Concurrent ingest of the same tenant+logical_name can race on `revision=next per tenant+name` despite ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (read-max-then-insert isn't atomic); needs SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or a DB-side sequence to keep the idempotency invariant.
  - Runtime DB role posture not stated: checklist 3 requires confirming the ingestion role is not BYPASSRLS/superuser and that BindTenant can't be bypassed; design only asserts RLS via the port.
  - Observability gap (checklist 10): only a CLI JSON report is specified — no metrics/log fields (ingest duration, bytes, drift count, failure reason) for the service; failures in scheduled/automated runs would be invisible.
  - `Head` checksum comparison assumes the object store surfaces sha256 on HEAD; if it does not (common for S3-compatible stores without checksum headers), `--verify` silently passes on the third leg. Design must specify the checksum source or fail closed when absent.
MINOR:
  - Registry targets are flipped to `exists`/`migrated` before any bytes are ingested (backfill_status=pending is honest, but `migration_status=migrated` with zero ingested objects over-claims); consider ordering the flip after a successful first `pfingest` run or documenting the semantics explicitly.
  - No `--dry-run`/report-only mode for `pfingest` (checklist 4); ingest isn't destructive, but operators need a pre-flight that shows planned writes without mutating.
  - Availability path unspecified: behavior when the object store or DB is down (retry/backoff, fail-closed, alert lead-time) is only implied by "fails closed" for size caps.
  - New standalone `go/intakeingest/go.mod` risks drifting from the repo's shared Go module/dependency pinning; confirm whether it should be a package in the existing module.
  - `store-registry` + `STORE-DATAFLOW.md` regeneration and the `gate0_check.py` path fix are two concerns in one item; the note says separate commit, but the design should bind the ordering so a revert doesn't strand generated docs.
NIT:
  - Content-addressed reuse means a reverted run leaves untracked objects; objreconcile orphan reporting is out of scope — ensure the report is actually emitted somewhere durable rather than only "reported".
  - `run_id` generation method (uuid vs timestamp) is unspecified; pin it in the schema doc to keep the pinned contract `pf.intake-ingest/1` stable.
  - Per-file status enum `skipped` should explicitly cover "unchanged + already verified" vs "unchanged but unverified" to avoid conflating idempotent skip with verify-pass.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid, reversible design that reuses existing ports, honors the language rule, and pre-empts over-claiming via backfill_status=pending.
  - Top risks: cross-tenant exposure at the raw object-key layer, a revision-allocation race undermining the idempotency AC, unverified assumptions about Head checksums, and thin observability for an operator-facing tool.
  - No blockers; resolve the MAJORs before Gate 1.5 sign-off.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present
